messages:
Olivia: quick brain-dump - thinking about a 'slice-first' refactor for continuous batching. instead of variable batches we form immutable slices (pack unit) and schedule slices. goal: simpler kv-cache pins + easier accounting. wanted quick sanity checks on tradeoffs.
Ben: Slice-first sounds cleaner. main worry is head-of-line on tiny slices - do we have tilt/hedging to avoid delaying small requests?
Olivia: yes, propose a small-requests fastpath: any slice under X tokens can be single-tenant fast-scheduled. otherwise slices are allowed to be mixed.
Maya: mixing is the tricky bit. we must ensure fair token accounting and eviction semantics when a slice contains multiple tenants. "slice_credit" ledger?
Sam: ledger idea good. two approaches: per-slice proportional credit or keep track per-tenant inside slice and charge p99 of slice completion to offenders. proportional feels easier for ops.
Priya: product note - customers want stable p95 and predictable billing. mixed slices that slow others will blow trust. default should favor isolation unless opt-in.
Olivia: agree. default: max_mixed_tenant_ratio = 0.15 and a conservative admission rule that rejects mixing if any tenant's outstanding_requests > threshold. enterprise flag to relax.
Ben: operationally, immutable slices simplifies kv-cache pinning as Maya said. if slice_id pins keys for N milliseconds, we can measure warmup cost. need tile-level (slice-level) metrics.
Maya: telemetry wishlist: slice.pack_density, slice.kv_warmups, slice.latency_p50/p95, slice.tenant_mix, slice.eviction_reason. also a gauge for slice_pending_count per-queue.
Sam: autoscaler effects: packed slices will spike GPU token throughput while user request rate may look flat. tag metrics: throughput.{raw, packed} so autoscaler can see normalized request rate.
Olivia: rough config prototype: 
``` 
# scheduler.slice
scheduler.slice.enabled = true
scheduler.slice.token_budget = 384
scheduler.slice.max_mixed_tenant_ratio = 0.15
scheduler.slice.fastpath_threshold = 64  # single-tenant immediate scheduling
scheduler.slice.pin_ttl_ms = 2500
scheduler.slice.latency_objective = "p95"
```
Ben: latency_objective is helpful - admission scoring can prefer low-variance slices for p95. do we compute score = alpha*p95_latency + beta*pack_density?
Olivia: yes, we can use a multi-objective score. initial alpha favors p95 for public tier, beta favors density for best-effort. knobs per-customer.
Maya: Implementation constraints: slices must be immutable after formation to avoid cache thrash. splitting on eviction is legal but expensive. prefer reject-on-mix until we validate.
Priya: timeline ask - can we try the conservative reject-on-mix for a 2-week experiment and collect telemetry? if results are good, unlock splitting for enterprise.
Sam: agree. also add a small e2e that simulates mixed tenants and measures p95 impact, kv-warmup cost, and autoscaler signals.
ci-bot: build/slice-refactor started - see CI: https://ci.redwood.example/slice-refactor/4960012345
Ben: ownership: Maya + Sam implement runtime + metrics, Olivia handles admission/score + config, Priya will draft product rollout + SLO language. I'll assist on infra checks.
Olivia: follow-up: i'll open RFC PR with diagrams and pseudo-code for slice lifecycle. plan a short demo Fri 9am.
Maya: one more note - consider proactive warming: when slice forms with cold kv keys, spawn a low-priority warm request to populate kv-cache before scheduling heavy mixed slices. reduces cold penalty.
Ben: warming looks promising but watch cost. perhaps only warm if expected pack_density > threshold.
Sam: logged an issue for autoscaler interplay: AUTOSCALE-4821. will add telemetry tags so scaling rules can ignore packed throughput if desired.
Priya: thanks all. if we keep defaults conservative we can move faster without upsetting customers. :thumbsup:
Olivia: thanks team, will post RFC link when ready. :rocket:
